title: A 'Pinch Me Moment': Kyle Clark Lands His Dream Netflix Lead in 'How to Ruin Diwali'
excerpt: The South African presenter-turned-actor stars opposite Rosemary Zimu-Mnguni in Netflix's three-episode Diwali comedy, premiering October 30 — a meet-the-parents clash of African and Indian families from the makers of the Kandasamys films.
body:
• Kyle Clark, best known as a South African TV presenter, plays Varshen, the fiancé at the centre of Netflix's How to Ruin Diwali: Meet the Parents, premiering October 30.
  • The three-episode comedy pairs him with Rosemary Zimu-Mnguni as Mmabatho, whose first meeting with his traditional Indian family over Diwali weekend spirals into chaos.
  • The series comes from Burnt Onion Productions with filmmaker Jayan Moodley of the Kandasamys franchise, and extends Netflix's How to Ruin Christmas and How to Ruin Love universe.
  • Clark says he deliberately toned down his presenter polish to play Varshen as real rather than a stereotype.

From presenter to leading man

Kyle Clark calls it a pinch-me moment. The South African television presenter has landed the male lead in How to Ruin Diwali: Meet the Parents, the newest instalment of Netflix's How to Ruin franchise, premiering October 30. In interviews around the trailer launch, Clark described the role as a dream part — and a deliberate departure: coming from a presenter background, he said he had to strip back the polish and play Varshen, an ordinary guy in an extraordinary family weekend, as authentically as he could rather than as a stereotype.

The setup: one dinner, two families, every secret out

The three-episode comedy centres on perfectionist Mmabatho, played by Rosemary Zimu-Mnguni, and her down-to-earth fiancé Varshen, who are ready to take the next step — except their families have never met. The introduction happens over Diwali weekend at the home of Varshen's parents, Tarina (Jailoshini Naidoo) and Sharm (Koobeshan Naidoo). It goes sideways fast, and the surprise arrival of Mmabatho's estranged parents, Penelope (Sonia Mbele) and Mandla (Meshack Mavuso), turns an awkward dinner into a collision of personalities, expectations and cultures — with one badly timed revelation threatening the whole celebration. The cast also includes Denise Zimba, reprising her role as Zama from How to Ruin Christmas, Luthando "BU" Mthembu, Ashish Gangapersad and Kaseran Pillay.

Clark and Zimu-Mnguni did a chemistry read early in casting; both have said the pairing felt right immediately, helped by a friendship that predates the show.

Why it matters beyond South Africa

The series is produced by Burnt Onion Productions with filmmaker Jayan Moodley, whose Kandasamys films built a mainstream audience for South African Indian family comedy. How to Ruin Diwali scales that formula to a global Netflix release in the middle of the Diwali season — an Indian festival as the setting, not a backdrop, for a meet-the-parents comedy about families who love each other badly and loudly. For diaspora viewers, it is also a rare streaming title where an Indian household's Diwali — the food, the rituals, the opinionated relatives — drives a story made for everyone. The trailer coverage is at Actor Spaces, and the leads' interview is at Sowetan. It premieres on Netflix on October 30, 2026.
